#1913. ‘Predictable, mutual, unfair’ - A brief history of Brighton’s sacked managers

So the current worst kept secret in football is out. Michael Carrick is no more at Old Trafford, it’s actually not United’s first rodeo in this footballing genre.

I recall being at the Amex on Easter Monday 2014, in the period of about 15 minutes I and four others in our party of ten that day received a forwarded text stating that David Moyes would be sacked as Manchester United manager the following morning, Tuesday 22nd April, and he was!

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Sackings are, unfortunately part and parcel of football. In my time following the Albion, we’ve had dismissals that have been predictable, justified, unfair and even a tad bizarre.

My first was Pat Saward in October 1973. I didn’t know much about, but in researching my book a couple of years ago, it was clear that once the ultra ambitious Albion chairman Mike Bamber got a sniff he might be able to rock the football world and bring Brian Clough to the Goldstone, dear old Pat was a dead man walking.

We then didn’t get another sacking for nearly a decade, and then it was all decided on the doorsteps of Sussex.

Mike Bailey had got the club it’s highest ever league finish, 13th in 81/82. But he was building from the back and at times the football wasn’t that exciting. Crowds dipped below the all important break even 15,000, and when fans were questioned by the lottery sellers on their weekly rounds, the word ‘boring’ was predominant and Bailey was out.

All these years later, I still believe the decision was a tad unfair and short sighted, but also one of those classic Brighton and Hove Albion sliding door moments.

Albion legend Steve Foster recently told me, whilst we probably wouldn’t have got to the 1983 Cup Final, we wouldn’t have got relegated and in time, Bailey could have turned us into a consistently top ten side, regularly challenging for Europe.

Bailey’s successor, Jimmy Melia, was almost in a footballing Sword of Damocles situation. Initially a caretaker boss, within a month the Albion embarked on an FA Cup campaign. With Bamber effectively waiting to wield the axe the Monday after the Albion were knocked out, but they weren’t. Melia, with his white dancing shoes took the Albion to Wembley but also rock bottom of the First Division and relegation!

Chris Cattlin was the next cab on the rank, his near three year tender, on a limited budget saw the Albion compete and again, like Bailey, given time, and funding, who knows what he could have achieved?

But he was unceremoniously dismissed at the end of the 85/86 season, but took the Albion to court for unfair dismissal, which resulted in his final victory at the club.

The returning Alan Mullery, another Goldstone legend, in the summer of 1986, was purely cosmetic. Replacing the popular Cattlin with the equally popular Mullery, saw a spike in season ticket sales, and not a lot more.

Mullery was a patsy, disgracefully treated when sacked in January 1987 for almost laughable reasons with the Albion in 13th.

A wretched run under new boss Barry Lloyd followed, with, as with the Division One exit in 1983, the Albion were relegated to the old Third Division in 22nd place in the division.

Yet we had to wait another nine years for another dismissal. Lloyd had left by mutual consent in December 1993, but in December 1996, with the cash strapped and soon to be homeless Albion in 92nd place in the Football League, Jimmy Case was unsurprisingly axed.

As was his successor, Steve Gritt, despite working a footballing miracle and keeping Albion in the league, he was gone in early 1998, again unjust, more about finance than football.

Exiled at Gillingham, crowds nowhere near break even, a massive shot in the arm was required, and that came in the shape of another returning legend (pattern forming) Brian Horton.

Jeff Wood, a genuinely nice guy, was in the wrong place at the wrong time Albion wise in 1999, as was Martin Hinshelwood in 2002.

Full disclosure, I’m in the privileged position to call a number of ex Albion bosses friends, and Mark McGhee is firmly in that catergory. His dismissal in September 2006, is another that sticks in the craw.

I do however still have a degree of sympathy in the bigger picture. At the time, Dick Knight, chasing our collective Falmer dream, was juggling all the balls whilst protecting his own.

Dean Wilkins, still in my opinion technically one of the best coaches the club has ever had, was both a safe pair of hands but a far cheaper option whilst the battle for the stadium went on, tellingly though however he has never worked as a manager since he departed the club in 2008.

I still believe that Mark McGhee would have mounted a promotion challenge to get us back in the Championship.

With the greatest respect in my opinion Albion wise Russel Slade still remains an irrelevance, only doing the job that Micky Adams would have done had he not resigned in February 2009.

Which brings us on to Gus Poyet, a footballing firework, it was great whilst it lasted, but it was what it was, and given off field working relationships, or lack of them, it was never going to last.

But to clarify Gus was not sacked live in the BBC, he was fully aware of the situation and his subsequent reaction was as genuine as American Wrestling!

But he still gave us some great memories, which will never be forgotten.

Chris Hughton’s sacking in 2019, was another exit, which leaves a bad taste. It could have been handled so much better. Like the Moyes text of 2014, I was told that Graham Potter was coming in 40 minutes before Hughton kicked off what was to be his final Albion game. Yet he was interviewed by Richie Reynolds on the pitch at the end about his hopes for the next season!

Potter, could and should have been sacked at least one or two occasions, but a crumb of comfort was the £20 million Chelsea gave us for his services, it truly is a funny old game.

So was Roberto De Zerbi sacked in May 2024, or merely his contract not renewed?

I still love his time as Albion manager, like Gus and others some amazing memories, but unfortunately there are boundaries and as soon as that microphone went under his nose in Rome with the apparent diatribe against Tony Bloom there was only going to be one outcome.

Which brings us around to Fab. Yes many, myself included, have embarked on the ‘Hurzeler Hokey Cokey’, but given the Albion’s current fortunes that’s well and truly parked.

You can never say never following the Albion but I think it’s a fairly safe bet there won’t be another Amex sacking anytime soon!

#1912. Bayern Munich transfer news: First contact made for Neuer successor in France

By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 10:39

Bayern Munich are thinking about life after Manuel Neuer and are looking for a long-term successor to their historic goalkeeper.

The 40-year-old is out of contract at the end of the season. The Bavarian club have explored several options, with two Ligue 1 goalkeepers on their shortlist: Kevin Trapp (Paris FC) and Lukas Hradecky (Monaco).

A third name can now be added: Robin Risser. According to information from Gianluca Di Marzio, Bayern Munich are taking a close interest in Risser’s profile. The Bavarian club have even made first contact and plan to step up their efforts soon.

The German giants already have a plan in mind to sign the Lens goalkeeper.

The Italian journalist says Bayern intend to sign the 21-year-old in the January transfer window, then loan him back to Lens for the second half of the season, before being able to count on him from next season. For the moment, no fee has emerged for this approach.

The advantage of this recruitment strategy is that it allows Risser to continue to progress at the northern club until the end of this season.

However, Bayern Munich are not alone in the race, as five other European heavyweights are interested: Manchester City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Inter Milan and Juventus. Lens are reportedly demanding at least £34m (€40m).

#1911. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

#1910. ‘Restricted’ - Mats Wieffer makes Brighton and Chema Andres claim as best position revealed

Brighton star Mats Wieffer admits he felt ‘restricted’ in the full back role as he targets a regular spot in central midfield.

The Dutch international joined Brighton as a midfielder for around £25m in 2024 but often played as a reluctant right full back.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It's a position Wieffer adapted to pretty well but now the former Feyenoord man is keen to make an impact in his preferred central midfield role.

Ferdi Kadioglu and Costinha are now the recognised right backs at Brighton, which means Wieffer can now compete for midfield minutes, alongside the likes of Pascal Gross, Yasin Ayari, Jack Hinshelwood, Diego Gomez and Chema Andres, who has impressed since his summer arrival.

Chema joined for around £20m from VfB Stuttgart and Wieffer feels they operate in a similar position.

Wieffer - who is fit once again following a recent knee injury - said to the club website: "I can still play both, but I'm happy to play in midfield.

"Now I need to keep the rhythm, train hard, and get all the principles there, because for the last two seasons I was more focused on full-back.

“I think Chema [Andres] and I are a little bit similar, but the rest are a little bit different. If I have to compare myself, I'm more like Chema than the others.”

He added: “You're always happy to play, but overall I prefer midfield because I've always done it. As a full-back, you're a little bit restricted, and I think I'm a better player as a midfielder overall.

“But last season went really well, and he always told me I was playing well and the system suited me. The stats were good, which gave me confidence that he put me in the starting XI.

“The team and playing are always the most important things for me. In the end I'm happy, but if I could choose I would play in midfield.”

Brighton are second in the table and resume Premier league action after the international break at Hull City.

It's been an impressive start to the season as Brighton have 22 points from 10 matches and are the division's leading scorers.

Wieffer said: “Last season we had the same kind of principles we have now, but this season we are doing it every game.

“When everybody sees that the things we train are working it gives the feeling that if we keep doing this it will pay off in points.

“Most importantly, it's because of the things we do like the pressing. Last season we didn't do it every game.

“In the bigger games we were always there but sometimes in the games we thought we needed to win it was a little bit less and opponents punished us.

“That was frustrating - getting points from a bigger team and then dropping points against a team we thought we were equals with.”

#1908. Unai Emery's grand plans for Aston Villa after agreeing new contract: Why he believes he can win Champions League, the Pep Guardiola blueprint and changing his mind on selling stars

Published: 07:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:54 EST, 12 November 2026

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson but when planning the current stage of his career the Spaniard had another boss in mind.

Having agreed a new contract that will make him one of the two best paid managers in the Premier League, Emery has the sort of structure at Villa that Pep Guardiola enjoyed for a decade at Manchester City.

Emery has always regarded Guardiola as the world’s best coach – and not just for the teams he has produced and the trophies he has won. The Basque admired Guardiola’s refusal to compromise on his vision for a club and has adopted those principles every step of the way at Villa, leading them from the bottom half to the Champions League.

‘We were speaking about how we can set our project stronger with a (new) deal, yes,’ Emery said last Friday, of a meeting he had with key figures at Villa including co-owner Nassef Sawiris a few days earlier. ‘Nassef is very ambitious, a hard worker and his commitment to the club is huge. It’s easy for me to have meetings with him as normally we are on the same page.’

This season began slowly but after six league games unbeaten, Villa are back in the top half and three points off the top five, as well as sitting sixth in the Champions League group phase with three wins from four.

After Emery underlined his desire to stay at Villa Park, Daily Mail Sport looks at what comes next for him and Villa.

Aston Villa hope Unai Emery will become their answer to Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares to extend his stay in the Midlands

After a slow start this season, Villa are in fine form in both the Premier League and Champions League

With about two-and-a-half years still remaining on Emery’s previous deal, there was no need for Sawiris to rush. His decision is both a show of faith and a recognition of the current climate.

Emery was on a five-man shortlist to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United but Daily Mail Sport understands he is unlikely to have moved to Old Trafford even without the contract discussions.

Studying Guardiola convinced Emery that to be successful, a manager needs control. He cannot operate if he has only limited influence over recruitment, or if he has no say in senior appointments – something United are highly unlikely to have granted.

Unlike at many clubs, where sporting directors and heads of performance are brought in by the chairman or chief executive, Emery has driven the key hires at Villa. Since Emery’s arrival, the number of Spanish backroom staff at Villa has grown well into double figures.

Director of football operations Damian Vidagany moved to Villa with Emery in 2022 and was a key reason why Emery accepted the job. Emery also pushed for Monchi to be brought in as ‘president of football operations’ and when that went wrong, he was allowed to select the next guy – Roberto Olabe. It is hard to imagine many other clubs where that would happen.

So far Olabe has been much better than his predecessor, whose dire record in the market saw him ditched a little more than a year ago.

Emery would have had none of this influence at United. In Sawiris, he has a highly supportive boss – contrast that with Sir Jim Ratcliffe. He makes the final calls on recruitment, rather than relying on the equivalent of Jason Wilcox.

Emery’s sense of self-worth is too great and his record too impressive to accept answering to executives of inferior ability. At Villa, he answers only to the ownership group, and he has forged a rock-solid relationship with Sawiris.

Emery was the driving force behind the appointments of director of football operations Damian Vidagany (left) and president of football operations Roberto Olabe (right)

Emery has a rock-solid relationship with co-owner Nassef Sawiris

There are few top clubs these days where the manager has a direct line to the owner but the Sawiris-Emery connection took shape in the autumn of 2022, weeks before he was hired. Sawiris could see the Steven Gerrard experiment was failing and wanted a top-class manager. He looked at Mauricio Pochettino, Thomas Tuchel and Emery.

After a difficult experience at Arsenal, Emery had won the Europa League with Villarreal and was assured by Sawiris that he would have the run of Villa. Emery felt he had never had this level of influence during his 18 months at Arsenal and throughout the process, Sawiris has been as good as his word.

Emery joined on just under £10million per year and his new salary would be close to double that. His wishes in the market have been backed, even when it has been tricky to make the sums add up. Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in January 2025 to deliver Champions League football. That did not happen, but there was no blowback for Emery because Sawiris trusted the direction of travel.

Every one of his requests has been approved. The current stadium redevelopment was planned for 2024 but was shelved because Emery did not wish to play Champions League games in a three-sided ground. Now, he has accepted the bigger picture.

At the training ground, a 40-room hotel was signed off on Emery’s say-so. When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi who took the rap, not Emery.

That sort of loyalty cuts both ways. With their stock so high, how many managers would have stuck around after six of their first-choice starting XI from a Europa League final win had been sold? Emery is taking a risk to his reputation by leading this rebuild but he trusts both himself and Sawiris to get it right.

Marcus Rashford and Marco Asensio were signed on loan at huge expense in 2025 to deliver Champions League football. There was no blowback for Emery when that did not happen

When Harvey Elliott was brought in on loan and then left in the cold, or when £26m signing Evann Guessand proved a mistake, it was Monchi (pictured) who took the rap, not Emery

There was a moment at the end of Friday’s press conference when Emery showed just how much he was invested in Aston Villa.

The Spaniard had just been asked if he could elevate Villa to the same level as Europe’s giants and instead of delivering the usual platitudes, Emery referred to the Deloitte Money League, which ranks clubs by the revenue they generate.

To emphasise his point, Emery grabbed his phone, found the page and confirmed that Villa had risen to 14th in the 2024-25 list, generating £376m in that period.

How many top-flight managers are even aware of the Deloitte Money League, let alone their club’s position in it? When asked about finances, most bosses will – quite legitimately – answer that these matters are for senior executives to handle.

Not Emery, who has made a definite shift in recent seasons. He now understands that because of Villa’s financial needs, part of his job will be to sign promising players, increase their value and then – potentially – sell them for double the fee.

This summer, Villa sold Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Ollie Watkins for a combined £253m. They were signed for a total of just £48m.

You can already picture Zion Suzuki and Johan Manzambi, two of the summer additions, falling into this category.

The unknown is how Emery might feel about this strategy in two or three years’ time if Villa slip out of contention for the Champions League.

Because for all the justifiable enthusiasm about a new contract, this will not be an easy road. Not surprisingly for an overhauled team, Villa are inconsistent.

Villa bought Morgan Rogers (fourth left), Ollie Watkins (fourth right), Ezri Konsa (right) and Youri Tielemans (not pictured) for a combined £48m, then sold them all this summer for £253m

You can already see Johan Manzambi - signed for £52m this summer - being the next player Villa make a huge profit from

After the Europa League triumph in May, Emery's dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa

Throw in their issues with financial regulations and the stadium rebuild and it would be no shock – nor any disgrace – if they finished outside the top five for the next couple of seasons.

Would that be enough for Emery, though? His dream is to win the Champions League and last week he made a strong case for saying he could do so with Villa.

Emery cited Leicester winning the Premier League and his own journey with Villarreal to the Champions League semi-finals in 2022.

Yet the rules are stacked in favour of the wealthiest and no matter how hard they try, Villa may never crack the code. By investing so heavily in Emery, though, Sawiris believes he is giving them a proper shot.

#1907. Jurgen Klopp loves him but Brajan Gruda may never play for Brighton again

Brajan Gruda arrived at Brighton in 2024 as one of Europe's hottest prospects.

Albion paid around £25m to Mainz for the German playmaker as he joined on a four-year contract.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"I saw the big impact he made in the Bundesliga and he's a player I admire a lot," said Brighton’s German head coach Fabian Hurzeler at the time.

Hurzeler also admired Gruda's style of play and describe the then 20-year-old as a "street footballer."

Jurgen Klopp used the same "street baller" term this week as Gruda - now 22 - made an impressive start to his senior Germany career.

He netted a fine individual goal on his full debut against Serbia last week and then grabbed a goal and two assists as Germany walloped the Netherlands 5-0 last night. Brighton's Bart Verbruggen was in goal for the Dutch.

After Gruda's excellent debut against Serbia, Klopp said he felt sorry for their left back Petar Sukacev. "That left-back, he's a poor lad!" said the former Liverpool boss Klopp.

Opta statistics backed up Klopp’s claim as they stated nine of Gruda's 14 dribbles against Serbia were successful.

"He's a fantastic player who loves to take people on and hasn't yet fulfilled his potential. He doesn't need to at his age, but he's shown an awful lot of positive signs," Klopp said.

So will he play for Brighton again and why did the Seagulls loan him out? Gruda made 45 appearances for Albion under Hurzeler in all competitions and showed glimpses of his potential with four goals and eight assists.

Niggling injuries and the fitness demands of the Premier League saw Gruda struggle to make a sustained impact. At times he featured in the No 10 role but largely he was behind the powerful Yankuba Minteh for the right wing slot.

Minteh joined for £30m in the same window as Gruda but the Gambian adapted faster. Gruda made just eight Premier League starts in the 2025-26 season and a change of environment was deemed beneficial by all parties and he joined RB Leipzig on loan for the second half of last campaign

“Brajan wants regular football, and we are not able to guarantee him that in the second half of the season," said Hurzeler.

Three goals and three assists for Leipzig in the Bundesliga convinced them to extend the loan for another season and Brighton were happy to sanction another temporary deal.

Sporting director Mike Cave said, “Brajan had a good second half of the season with Leipzig and was keen to explore the opportunity of remaining there for the coming year.

“This is a move that allows Brajan to continue to secure regular playing time at a good level, in an environment he knows well.”

Brighton are pretty sharp on their loan agreements but no doubt they will now be double checking the small print of the loan contract.

Leipzig are believed to have an obligation to buy at the end of the season, albeit with certain conditions - but the size of any potential transfer fee remains unclear.

His value is clearly going upwards and the loan agreement will likely allow Brighton to cash in, should they decide to sell. Further high-profile displays for Klopp's Germany will see that increase.

Gruda remains contracted with Albion until 2028 and this week Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen were also credited with interest.

Transfer expert Florian Plettenberg posted: “The obligation to buy for Brajan Gruda will be activated in 2027 due to accounting reasons. The total package for RB Leipzig will amount to €30m, including bonuses. Gruda will then get a contract until 2031, which has already been agreed.

“Bayern have always had him on their list, even before his move to Brighton. However, he is currently not a concrete transfer target for Bayern – unless something extraordinary happens, such as the sale of Michael Olise.”

Gruda seems to prefer living and playing his football in Germany and whether he even considers moving back to Brighton remains to be seen. The Seagulls - who are flying high in the Premier League - also have a number of options on the right flank.

Minteh - who almost joined Liverpool last summer - is just returning from injury, while Paraguayan international Diego Gomez has also excelled in the wide right position this term.

Zadok Yohanna, Femi Azeez, Malick Yalcouye are all available, while the likes of Amario Cozier-Duberry and Harry Howell are out on loan.

Gruda's form is impressive but whether he returns to the Premier League with Brighton anytime soon is debatable. Attention will now likely turn to maximising their fee.

#1905. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

#1897. Mauricio Pochettino should TURN DOWN the Man United job unless he gets TWO new signings to fix 'the worst back four in the Premier League', says Gary Neville

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:19 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 10:08 EST, 12 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino has been warned against taking the Manchester United job, by Gary Neville unless the club's hierarchy promise to back him in the January transfer window and bolster 'the worst back four in the Premier League'.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport, Pochettino is expected to be named as the new Red Devils head coach, replacing Michael Carrick. Carrick was pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning before being sacked just hours later.

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning too. He had been in Monaco the day before with the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe ratified their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Upon Pochettino's expected arrival, he will join a club languishing in the relegation zone - with United 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 matches.

United have conceded 19 goals across those 10 games - with only 14th-placed Ipswich Town (20) and bottom side Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) has been warned against becoming the new Manchester United head coach by Gary Neville unless they promise him defensive reinforcements in January

Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington on Thursday morning ahead of his Man United sacking

Director of football Jason Wilcox was pictured arriving to the club's training ground on Thursday morning after being in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's fate at the club

And speaking about Pochettino's pending arrival, Neville insists on the Argentine making ultimatums to the board if they want him - starting with improving the defence.

'If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven,' he said on The Overlap.

'He'll do that with a pay-off. So do that in your contract. But secondly, he needs two defenders in January. So he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January. He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer we're not to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

'They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.'

Expanding further, the former United right back didn't hold back in his criticism of the current defensive options at the club.

'I mean look the back four that he finished with on Sunday was [Diogo] Dalot left back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,' he said.

'That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.'

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

Neville believes Manchester United have 'the worst back four in the Premier League'

Diogo Dalot (left) gave away a penalty during United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and Pochettino may even would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession plan in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

The 54-year-old only signed a new deal after the World Cup meaning that United could have got him for nothing in the summer.

Alexander's partnership with assistant Chris Lucketti was a winning one, with coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle also being key components to the Bantams' upturn.

Duff, whose side are preparing for back-to-back home league derbies with Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley, said: "Truey's been in the club for a long time and worked under a few managers.

He acknowledges that his deputy is particularly important for daily dialogue with players, as his assistant position allows him to develop a more up-close-and-personal relationship.

The City boss continued: "Alex spends a lot more time with the players than I do because he's around them a lot more often and they'll probably have more personal conversations with Alex. It's something he's very good at.

"I try to, but obviously sometimes when you speak to a player, it's like: 'Well, he's the headmaster, so tell him what he wants and get out,' which I don't want it to be like that. But that's just the natural evolution of my job.

"Alex is good for many different reasons. Tactically, he's very, very good and has been coaching for a long, long time.

"He's coached at a high level. He's worked with League Two players and worked at Championship level, so he can put on different sessions and knows what the group needs and knows me as well.

"Sometimes that's where assistants are really good, because it's like: 'I know you want to do this, but this might not be right at the moment'. And that's where sometimes I have to check my own ego, because it's not about me.

"He's a really good sort of sounding board because he knows me really well."

#1894. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

#1890. Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku announces shock retirement from international football

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05

Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has announced that he has retired from international football.

With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.

Lukaku's most recent outing for Belgium was against France on November 5, the 33-year-old donning the captain's armband on that occasion.

However, Lukaku did not play in Belgium's last two fixtures, being ruled out versus Turkey last Thursday due to a hip injury and remaining as an unused substitute for Sunday's 4-1 victory over Italy.

On Monday morning, Lukaku took to social media to make the surprise revelation that he had called time on his international career.

A statement on Instagram read: "Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team…I experienced every emotion imaginable…

"I was lucky enough to play alongside extraordinary teammates, to whom I will always be grateful. I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches who pushed me to give my best and trusted me to help the team. It was a wonderful journey, and I cherished every moment.

"To the Belgian fans, thank you for all the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was incredible. I enjoyed it immensely. I am grateful. Thank you."

Under both Rudi Garcia at the World Cup and Mark van Bommel across the six recent UEFA Nations League matches, Lukaku has not been viewed as a certain starter.

That is despite the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scoring in four of his last seven outings for his country.

While Lukaku has not shed light on any potential issues behind the scenes, an assumption can be made that remaining as an unused substitute in two of the five games that he was available under Van Bommel has played its part.

At the age of 33, Lukaku had the opportunity to join a list of players who have reached 100 goals for their country. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Ali Daei have achieved that feat.

Choosing to stay six goals short of the illustrious three figures feels an unusual choice on Lukaku's part, but it does not take away from ending his international career with 53 goals more than any other Belgian player in history.

The 27-year-old has won 64 caps for his country, scoring 25 goals, and was in action as Germany beat Serbia 3-1 on Friday.

The former Chelsea man will be in the team on Monday night for the crucial Nations League clash with Netherlands, as Klopp looks to take his side into the quarter-finals.

The Germany boss has looked to build confidence in Havertz by talking up the forward’s qualities, which he feels can match up to almost anyone in the game.

‘I have often faced teams defended by Kai, and I know very well in tactical preparations that facing Kai is not an easy task. He is a complete package as a top player,’ said Klopp.

‘Mikel Arteta relies heavily on him because Kai is always reliable to put in an extraordinary performance thanks to his technical capacity and intelligence.’

He added: ‘Kai and I have agreed that there is still huge potential that we want to develop further together in the national team.’

Havertz has not been in good goal-scoring form of late, netting just once in his last 13 appearances for club and country.

That was a crucial goal in a 1-0 Arsenal win over Liverpool, but finding the back of the net has not come easily for the Gunners star.

He will look to improve his recent record in Berlin on Monday night as Germany try and topple the group-leaders, although Klopp says the long-term project is more important than short-term success.

‘We want success right now, but the process we have set in motion takes precedence over everything else,’ he said.

‘We want to put in a top performance, then we will see how that measures up against the Netherlands.

‘We are really looking forward to this game. We wanted this opportunity, now we have got it and we want to make the most of it.

‘[Netherlands have] basically got the same squad that played at the World Cup, that is the difference between us. We are in a period of transition right now.’

#1884. Why Man United decided against appointing Didier Deschamps as their new head coach

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 11:52, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 11:55

Manchester United had reportedly considered Didier Deschamps as a replacement for Michael Carrick, but conversations with the Frenchman and his representatives over a move to Old Trafford 'did not go well'.

Carrick was sacked by Man United last week due to the team's struggles in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been appointed at his replacement, with the Argentine due to officially take charge on November 18.

In the latter stages of Carrick's time at Old Trafford, there were suggestions that Deschamps was being seriously considered as a replacement for the Englishman.

According to The Athletic, contact was made over a potential move for the 58-year-old, who stepped down as France head coach following the 2026 World Cup.

However, the report claims that the conversations 'did not go well'.

Man United allegedly believed that Deschamps was looking to gain leverage for a move to manage in Saudi Arabia.

Deschamps has been in charge of Monaco, Juventus and Marseille during his club management career, while he was France's boss between 2012 and 2026.

The former midfielder guided Monaco to success in the Coupe de la Ligue, in addition to overseeing a spot in the 2003-04 Champions League final.

Deschamps also lifted the Serie B title in 2006-07 while in charge of Juventus, in addition to Ligue 1, three Coupe de la Ligue trophies and two Trophee des Champions while at Marseille.

For France, Deschamps guided the team to the 2018 World Cup and 2020-21 UEFA Nations League trophies, in addition to helping the Blues reach the final of Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup.

Deschamps is thought to be in line for a move to Saudi Arabia at some stage in the near future.

Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were also all linked with the role at Old Trafford before Pochettino's arrival was confirmed.

Pochettino will be aiming to make the perfect start to life at Man United when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League this weekend.

#1882. Leeds United and Hull City’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace confirm Thomas Frank appointment

Leeds United and Hull City’s Premier League rivals Crystal Palace have unveiled Thomas Frank as their new manager.

The Eagles dispensed of the services of Pierre Sage last week, dismissing him after a run of four consecutive league defeats.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has been replaced by Frank, who has previously led Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur, and has now taken charge of a London club for the third time.

Frank said: “It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

“Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.”

Frank has quite the job on his hands, with Palace rooted to the bottom of the Premier League table after just two wins in 10 games.

Just above them in the relegation zone, in 19th and 18th respectively, are Sunderland and Manchester United.

Eagles chairman Steve Parish said: “I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace. He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”

Frank will take charge of Palace for the first time this weekend, when they will visit Frank Lampard’s Coventry City. His first home game as boss is scheduled for November 29, when Hull are due to make the trip to Selhurst Park.

Paddy McCarthy will remain on the books as a coach having assisted Sage, while the Eagles have also retained goalkeeping coach and Frank’s former Brentford colleague Andy Quy.

#1881. Martin Zubimendi stance on Chelsea transfer as Arsenal set asking price

Martin Zubimendi is seriously considering leaving Arsenal for the first time and has refused to rule out a move to Chelsea, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game for Arsenal this season, with the concerning lack of game-time sparking speculation over his future at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spanish midfielder enjoyed a bright start to his Gunners career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad, earning rave reviews from Mikel Arteta this time last year.

But Zubimendi had lost his place in the Arsenal team by the end of the season, with a teenage Myles Lewis-Skelly instead starting the Champions League final against PSG.

The 27-year-old has continued to struggle for minutes this season and is now, for the first time, considering his future at the club.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Spanish outlet AS say Zubimendi has his eye on a January exit and is ‘open to everything’ following reports linking him with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

Xabi Alonso is keen to strengthen his midfield options and knows Zubimendi well from his previous spell at Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi is contracted to Arsenal until 2030 but reports in Spain say the north London club will consider offers for the World Cup winner of at least £60m.

Last week, Zubimendi was forced to address speculation linking him with a move away from Arsenal while on international duty with Spain.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens.

‘I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Zubimendi also revealed he was warned about a possible lack of minutes by Arteta ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

Arteta bolstered his midfield options over the summer, with Arsenal spending £75m to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,’ Zubimendi added. ‘As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

‘It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too. Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

‘I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

Middlesbrough legend Tony Mowbray has stepped back from his role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers due to health issues.

The 62-year-old, who represented Middlesbrough with disinction as a player and later as their manager, took the reins at Ewood Park in the summer.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He has steered Rovers into 13th place in the Championship, defying low pre-season expectations, but has now stepped aside.

Mowbray said: “Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers. I’m immensely proud of this group of players.

“Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

“Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you. To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

Blackburn’s owner B. Balaji Rao said: “Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

“Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.”

#1879. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham England Under-21 record

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’

#1878. When will Thomas Frank take charge of first Crystal Palace game? Eagles ‘finalising’ appointment of Pierre Sage replacement

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:32, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 12:34

Crystal Palace are reportedly close to appointing Thomas Frank as their new head coach.

The Eagles appear to be moving quickly to replace Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

It had previously been reported that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage, while the likes of Anthony Barry, Vitor Pereira, Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss Frank has now been identified as the leading candidate to take the reins at Selhurst Park, with ‘advanced talks’ held over the weekend.

The Athletic have since claimed that Palace are finalising an agreement to appoint Frank, who is expected to become the club’s new head coach.

Talks are said to be ongoing over Frank’s backroom staff and an official announcement of his arrival in South London is set to follow in due course.

All being well, Frank could potentially take charge of his first Crystal Palace game on Saturday when they travel to Coventry City in the Premier League.

If Frank is not appointed before the weekend, then the Dane could instead make his Palace debut in the Europa League when the Eagles play host to Real Sociedad on November 26.

The 53-year-old is set to return to management for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham in February after only eight months in charge.

Frank won just 13 of his 38 matches with Spurs and left the club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

He had previously enjoyed a successful seven-year spell as Brentford boss between 2018 and 2025, steering the Bees into the top flight and then establishing them as a competitive Premier League outfit, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

In June, Frank stated that he had no intentions to take a new managerial position, but he now appears to be ready to return to the dugout and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

Frank will be tasked with lifting the Eagles off the foot of the Premier League table following a run of seven defeats in 10 games at the start of this season under Sage, conceding a division-high 24 goals in the process.

However, victory over Coventry this weekend could see Palace climb out of the relegation zone and up to 16th in the table if other results were to go their way.

#1875. Origi recalls how Milan tenure turned sour: “We weren’t on the same page”

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

Origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was quickly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

In short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

“At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a new challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

“Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”

“I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

“There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”

“I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

#1873. EFL asks clubs to stop targeted 'banter' on social media amid fears over reputational damage in the wake of 'Spygate' fallout

Published: 09:54 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 11:40 EST, 12 November 2026

The EFL has written to clubs calling for a halt in reputationally damaging social media posts disguised as ‘banter’ - believing the line has been blurred when it comes to regulatory matters.

The letter expressed concern over a ‘growing pattern of posts that use disputes, disciplinary matters, alleged wrongdoing or rival Clubs as material for public “banter”.’

A letter, seen by Daily Mail Sport, has been sent by EFL chief executive Trevor Birch to club chairs and executives following a board meeting.

‘While any one post may be viewed as an isolated lapse, taken together they risk creating a culture in which short-term engagement is prioritised over judgement, responsibility and long-term reputation,’ the letter read.

‘This is not about removing humour, personality or rivalry from Club channels. It is about recognising when content becomes disparaging, prolongs a dispute, targets an individual, or calls the integrity of a Club or the competition into question.

‘The impact extends beyond the Clubs directly involved. Repeated public exchanges can inflame relationships, undermine confidence in the fairness and professionalism of our competitions, and weaken the collective EFL brand.

The EFL have called for clubs to halt 'banter' social media posts. Pictured: Wrexham owners Rob Mac (left) and Ryan Reynolds (right) spoofed Southampton's Spygate case in September. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Wrexham were among the clubs to mock the case by putting a not to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors' prior to their match with Southampton on fixture release day. Source: X/Wrexham_AFC

Birmingham City also referenced the case by revealing the date for their fixture by showing the club badges cut into hedges and visible through binoculars. Source: X/BCFC

‘Recent media interest in perceived public disputes between Clubs illustrates how quickly individual posts can become a wider reputational issue.’

Daily Mail Sport understands the EFL are keen to avoid being seen as killjoys. Rather, they are taking a preventative approach to posts that could end up breaching FA or EFL rules.

The Southampton ‘Spygate’ scandal is among the most prominent disputes that have been referenced by clubs in social media content in recent months.

Both Birmingham City and Wrexham shared posts on the Championship fixture release date in June, using the case to highlight the dates of a fixture with Southampton.

Birmingham’s official X account posted a graphic of both clubs' badges cut into hedges which were viewed through binoculars. The account added: ‘One of the other key fixtures to keep an eye on...’

Wrexham’s calendar for their matches in September included a reminder to 'check training ground for unauthorised visitors’ two days before they played Southampton. An image of a man behind a tree was included in the Southampton badge.

The club also included their Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac in a spoof video in the build-up to the match. The actors were seen behind a tree similar to one which Southampton intern William Salt was caught spying near ahead of their play-off semi-final with Middlesbrough.

Following the revelations by Daily Mail Sport, Southampton were eventually thrown out of the play-offs.

Last week, Blackburn hit back at a video of West Ham manager Scott Parker declaring he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan’ by showing images of their supporters celebrating goals in their 2-1 win over the Hammers.

Blackburn hit back at West Ham boss Scott Parker last week after he declared he ‘didn’t see a Blackburn fan', with the club then showing supporters celebrating goals. Source: X/Rovers

The EFL reminded clubs in their letter that regulations called for clubs to ‘to act towards one another with utmost good faith’. The organisation called for clubs to consider whether their content is ‘punching down’ or ‘targeting a specific Club or individual’, adding they would likely cross the threshold if it does.

The organisation stressed that its preference is for ‘engagement and prevention’ and was not requesting clubs to make ‘bland or risk-free’ content.

However, the EFL warned it is prepared to take ‘proportionate and consistent action’ where ‘conduct which doesn’t meet the standards we expect is repeated or serious.’

Clubs have been asked to ensure a senior leader owns the standard applied to the club’s content, as well as formalising approval arrangements, briefing relevant people and exercising restraint.

#1872. Jesus Owono’s punishment criticised following death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra owner Gerard Pique says Jesus Owono ‘does not deserve’ the 12-game suspension he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The footballing world was rocked earlier this month as it was announced that De Miguel had tragically passed away at the age of 30 after he was involved in a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono.

Owono had raced out of goal in the closing stages of the Spanish second-tier contest before clattering into De Miguel, whose severe head and chest injuries caused him to go into cardiac arrest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the centre-forward’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated – and he died the following day.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the days and weeks that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Last week, Owono learned that he would be banned for Andorra’s next 12 matches for the role he played in the deadly collision, with the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee stating that the player had ‘violently struck an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

It went on: ‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

The statement added that the ‘nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances’ meant that the ‘maximum sanction’ was ‘justified’.

It was also confirmed that the match involving Andorra and Tenerife – which was called off when the teams were locked at 2-2 deep into stoppage time – would not be replayed.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘This avoids having to resume play from the precise moment at which the tragic incident occurred,’ it read.

Owono’s suspension has received a mixed reaction in Spain, with some feeling it too lenient while others have called for the ‘distressed’ goalkeeper to be given greater support.

According to Andorra owner Pique, the former Barcelona, Manchester United and Spain defender, Owono is ‘not to blame’ for the tragic outcome of the deadly collision.

‘I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve,’ he said in a statement.

‘He is not to blame for all of this having happened.’

Pique pointed to a separate incident earlier this month in Spanish football, when Albacete attacker Jose Corpas accidentally kicked Sabadell’s Quadri Liameed in the head during a second-tier encounter.

‘Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,’ Pique added.

‘With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?’

Pique, a World Cup winner with Spain in 2010, made it clear that Owono would likely require a significant break away from the game before being able to compete again.

‘Jesus is going to need far more than 12 matches before he is available and able to play,’ he continued.

‘No sanction is going to bring De Miguel back to us.’

Tenerife’s grieving squad returned to action for the first time since De Miguel’s death against Cueta on Sunday.

Goals from Nacho Gil and Neal Viereck sealed Tenerife a 2-0 victory on an emotional day the club’s Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez.

#1870. Spain 2-3 England: Thomas Tuchel’s side set new all-time winning record after “complete performance” in Nations League

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 13:21

England have set a new all-time winning record after beating world champions Spain 3-2 in their final UEFA Nations League group fixture on Sunday.

The Three Lions knew that they had to beat the 2026 World Cup winners at Estadio Metropolitano on Madrid if they were to finish top of League A Group 3 on goal difference.

Thomas Tuchel’s side entered the half-time interval in front courtesy of a converted penalty from 2026 Ballon d’Or winner and England’s top goalscorer Harry Kane, who has set yet another scoring record.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased England’s lead with two goals in the space of just four minutes, putting the visitors firmly in control.

However, Elliot Anderson was sent off just six minutes after England’s third goal for a last-man pull-back on Lamine Yamal inside the penalty area, with Mikel Oyarzabal netting the resulting spot kick.

The momentum then shifted into Spain’s favour and substitute Nico Williams gave the hosts hope of a late comeback with a 75th-minute strike, but the Three Lions admirably dug deep to hold on for a crucial victory.

Victory for England means they have now won 10 consecutive away matches across all competitions for the first time in their history.

Success has also confirmed that England finish top of League A Group 3, progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals where they will face one of the runners-up in League A, with a guaranteed second leg at home.

Furthermore, England’s memorable night in Madrid saw them end Spain’s world-record 43-game unbeaten run spanning across almost three years.

After the match, Tuchel acknowledged that his team’s performance against La Roja was their best since he became England head coach in January 2025.

“Yes,” he told reporters. “Given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. That was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

“What a performance we put out there to be deservedly 3-0 up after 60 to 65 minutes. Of course the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes [of defending] against Spain in Spain feels like three hours!

“This was, of course, a statement victory and the statement and significance of it was that it was deserved.

“The result followed the performance. It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, on all aspects of the game.

“We did everything that needs to be done together – the deep buildup, the high press and attacking defensive phases.

England’s next match will be the first leg of their Nations League quarter-final tie, scheduled between March 25 and March 27 next year.

The Three Lions will discover their opponent when the draw is made on Friday at 11am UK time.

England cannot be drawn against Spain again, but they could face Group A1 runners-up Belgium, or one of three teams from Group A2 (Netherlands, Greece or Germany) or Group A4 (Portugal, Denmark or Norway).

The official quarter-final lineup will be confirmed after the final round of fixtures on Tuesday.

#1867. Spain 2-3 England: Harry Kane equals 78-year Tom Finney scoring record in Nations League win

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:20

England captain Harry Kane has etched his name into the record books once again after scoring in Sunday’s 3-2 triumph over Spain in the UEFA Nations League.

The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner made his 127th international appearance at Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, just three days after surpassing Peter Shilton as England’s most-capped player against Croatia.

On the stroke of half time, Kane fired England into a deserved half-time lead with a converted penalty after being felled by Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

In doing so, England’s No.9 has now equalled an impressive scoring feat which had been unmatched since 1948.

Indeed, Kane has scored in each of his last seven international away matches dating back to June 2025, becoming the first Three Lions player to achieve this feat since legend Tom Finney between September 1946 and May 1948.

This record excludes neutral venues and therefore does not include the goals Kane scored at the 2026 World Cup where England finished third.

Kane’s away scoring streak began with goals in four successive World Cup qualifiers against Andorra, Serbia, Latvia and Albania, helping the Three Lions complete their qualification campaign with a perfect record.

The Bayern Munich striker has since netted in all three of his away matches with England in the Nations League against Czech Republic, Croatia and now Spain.

Kane has scored a total of 10 goals across those seven away games, while he has also extended his all-time scoring record with England to 93.

The last time Kane failed to make the net ripple for England at a non-neutral away venue came against Greece in November 2024 (3-0 Nations League win).

Kane will endeavour to surpass Finney outright and extend his scoring run on the road to eight games when England enter the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Reacting to England’s memorable win in Madrid, Kane told reporters: “I think that’s as big as it gets outside of a major tournament, for sure.

“We spoke before the Nations League campaign that we want to use these games to really improve, really stamp our identity on how we want to move going forward.

“No better game than Spain away after they’re unbeaten in 40-odd games to show that, and what a performance. Up until the red card it was dominant, clinical, high intensity and they couldn’t live with it.

“It was a shame [Elliot Anderson’s] red card happened because I think [the scoreline] could have been more and that’s been our mindset. That it doesn’t matter what the scoreline is – we go and we go and we go. You saw that out there tonight.

“In the end, we had to find a different way to win with the red card, obviously, and it was similar to a Mexico feeling where we’re digging deep.

“But when you can do both sides of the game like that it means you’re a very good team, so credit to everyone involved. It’s been a great campaign so far and we can end the year with our heads held high.”

Kane has scored in all six of England’s Nations League matches in the 2026-27 campaign, netting a competition-high eight goals in total to put him firmly in the frame to win the Golden Boot.
